To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the least effective teacher is perceived as less competent on the three dimensions of teacher competency, but that the most effective teacher is perceived to have the greatest competency in the dimension of technical proficiency.

the most effective teacher is perceived to be more competent in all three dimensions of competency; the most effective teacher has the least deficiencies in all three dimensions; and the most effective teacher’s deficiencies are in the interpersonal relations and teaching technique dimensions.

industrial arts supervisors judge teachers as more competent in the technical dimension, that the most and least effective teacher have different perceptions of their own effectiveness, and that the least effective teacher is perceived as having more deficiencies in interpersonal relations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a device to measure teacher competency in industrial arts.
a study of the relationship of industrial arts teachers' competency to their effectiveness.
the relationship of the three competency dimensions to the supervisors’ judgments of effectiveness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most effective teacher was perceived to be more competent in all three dimensions.

the most effective teacher is rated higher in all three dimensions than the least effective teacher, but the most effective teacher’s greatest strengths are in teaching techniques and technical proficiency while the least effective teacher’s greatest weaknesses are in interpersonal relations, teaching technique and technical proficiency.
the supervisors in this study perceived teachers as more technically proficient than they did as being competent on the interpersonal relations and teaching technique dimensions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most effective teacher is judged as being more competent in all three dimensions.
the least effective teacher was deficient in the three dimensions.
the supervisors’ judgments of effectiveness are significantly related to their judgments of the teachers’ competencies on the three dimensions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
supervisors can make judgments about teacher competence and effectiveness, and these judgments are related.
the most effective teachers have a better command of teaching techniques and interpersonal relations.
the most effective teacher is perceived to be more technically proficient, and the least effective teacher to be deficient in interpersonal relations and technical proficiency.
